label: Person
name: Adalsinda
summary:
Adalsinda (c. 620–c. 680) was a Frankish noblewoman and abbess associated with the Columban monastic tradition in seventh-century Gaul. She is venerated as a saint in the Catholic tradition and represents the remarkable generation of Merovingian aristocratic women who embraced the radical asceticism of the Irish-Columban tradition introduced by Columbanus of Bobbio.

The Columban movement had an extraordinary impact on Merovingian Gaul. Columbanus's foundation of Luxeuil (590) became the centre of a monastic network that spread across Frankish territory with extraordinary speed, fed by the enthusiasm of Merovingian nobles — both men and women — who found in Irish-style monasticism a form of radical Christian commitment that the older Gallic monastic tradition had not provided. Women like Adalsinda founded or led communities that combined ascetic rigour with aristocratic prestige.

Her veneration reflects the broader phenomenon of seventh-century Frankish female sanctity — a generation so rich in holy women that historians have called it the 'golden age' of Merovingian women's religious life. These women — Radegund, Balthild, Gertrude of Nivelles, Rictrude of Marchiennes — combined royal or noble birth with genuine spiritual depth, and their monasteries became centres of culture and healing that served their surrounding communities.
